definitions.standard: Two or more forms of the same element that contain equal numbers of protons but different numbers of neutrons in their nuclei.
definitions.simple: Atoms of the exact same element that weigh different amounts because they have a different number of neutrons inside.
definitions.scientific: Nuclides having the same atomic number (number of protons) but different mass numbers (number of neutrons).

linguistics.origin: From Greek 'isos' (equal) + 'topos' (place), meaning 'the same place' (in the periodic table).

advanced_data.history: Term introduced by Frederick Soddy in 1913.

common_misconceptions: Isotopes of an element have different chemical properties. (They do NOT. They have the same chemical properties because they have the same number of electrons).
tutor_context.tutor_hint: Think of isotopes like identical twins where one twin ate a bit more food and is heavier. They are still the same person (element), just a different weight!
